label: New Jersey-regulated plan
summary: Your plan appears to be regulated by New Jersey. After the plan’s internal appeal, New Jersey’s Independent Health Care Appeals Program (IHCAP) can send your case to an independent reviewer.

regulator.name: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance (DOBI)

source.title: Consumer Assistance & Insurance Complaints
source.authority: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance

claims.text: For most job-based and individual health plans, you get at least 180 days after receiving a denial to file an internal appeal.

sources.title: Claims procedure for employee benefit plans (ERISA)
sources.authority: U.S. Department of Labor, Employee Benefits Security Administration

claims.text: HealthCare.gov says an internal appeal must be decided within 30 days for care you haven’t received yet, and within 60 days for care you already received.
IHCAP generally requires you to finish the plan’s internal appeal first.

sources.title: Independent Health Care Appeals Program (IHCAP)
sources.authority: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance

claims.text: NJ DOBI says a standard IHCAP decision takes no more than 45 calendar days from when the appeal is submitted.

sources.title: Independent Health Care Appeals Program (IHCAP)
sources.authority: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance

claims.text: HealthCare.gov says your insurer is required by law to accept the external reviewer’s decision.
New Jersey’s Independent Health Care Appeals Program (IHCAP) does not accept appeals for self-funded plans, Medicare, Medicare Advantage, or insurance contracts delivered in another state.

sources.title: Independent Health Care Appeals Program (IHCAP)
sources.authority: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance

claims.text: For problems with a New Jersey-regulated insurer, NJ DOBI’s Consumer Hotline is 1-800-446-7467.

sources.title: Consumer Assistance & Insurance Complaints
sources.authority: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance

uncertainties: NJ DOBI’s IHCAP page doesn’t state a deadline for requesting external review. Use the deadline in the plan’s final internal appeal decision, and confirm it with NJ DOBI.
how_to_confirm: Look at your insurance card. Medicare, Medicare Advantage, and NJ FamilyCare cards say so.

Check your plan documents (the Summary Plan Description or Summary of Benefits and Coverage) for the words “self-funded,” “self-insured,” “fully insured,” “ERISA,” or “grandfathered,” and for the state where the policy was issued.
If you get coverage through work, ask HR: “Is our health plan self-funded or fully insured, and which state issued the policy?”
Call the member services number on your card and ask who regulates your plan.
